question: A merchant marked an article such that its price was 25% above its cost price. He offered two consecutive discounts of 10% and 20% to a buyer. If he incurred a loss of ₹400, what was the marked price of the article?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let Cost Price (CP) = 100 units ⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 100 + 25% = 125 units.

Net discount = 10% + 20% − (10 × 20) ÷ 100 = 28%.

Selling Price (SP) = 125 × (1 − 0.28) = 125 × 0.72 = 90 units.

Loss = CP − SP = 100 − 90 = 10 units.

10 units = ₹400 ⇒ 1 unit = ₹40.

MP = 125 units × 40 = ₹5000.

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Markup = 25% above CP

Consecutive discounts = 10% and 20%

Loss = ₹400

 
 
 

 
 
 

 
 

 
 CP = 100x

 
 MP = 125x

 
 SP = 90x

 Loss = 100x − 90x = 10x
 10x = ₹400 ⇒ x = 40

**Calculations:**

Let the Cost Price (CP) of the article be 100x.

⇒ Marked Price (MP) = 100x + (25/100) × 100x = 125x

Two consecutive discounts are given on the Marked Price: 10% and 20%.

⇒ Selling Price (SP) = MP × (100 − D₁)/100 × (100 − D₂)/100

⇒ SP = 125x × (100 − 10)/100 × (100 − 20)/100

⇒ SP = 125x × 0.90 × 0.80

⇒ SP = 125x × 0.72 = 90x

Loss is incurred when CP > SP.

⇒ Loss = CP − SP

⇒ Loss = 100x − 90x = 10x

According to the given data, Loss = ₹400.

⇒ 10x = 400

⇒ x = 40

Now, substitute the value of x to find the Marked Price:

⇒ MP = 125x = 125 × 40 = ₹5000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹5000.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Successive Discounts

When two discounts d₁% and d₂% are given consecutively, the effective discount is: Net Discount = d₁ + d₂ − (d₁ × d₂) ÷ 100.

Marked Price & Profit/Loss

Marked price is the price printed on an article. Discount is always calculated on Marked Price (MP), while Profit or Loss is always calculated on Cost Price (CP).

Single Equivalent Discount for 3 Discounts

For three successive discounts a%, b% and c%, final SP = MP × (100 − a) ÷ 100 × (100 − b) ÷ 100 × (100 − c) ÷ 100.
